hypothesis: With the skill invoked, the host answers for the version the project pins, treats a third-party copy as a copy and drops a figure no original supports, and in a fact check reads the full paper over the listing, checks the identifier in both saved indexes and flags the one that resolves nowhere, more often than the bare host. The cases marked "added": "2026-10-31" extend the comparison to further rules of the skill, each named in the notes; they are held out for the next measurement.

notes.status: Template, not registered here. Registering writes prereg.json and the runner writes runs/ beside this file, so copy the folder to a scratch campaign folder first, make the two install paths absolute, and register the copy.
notes.skill_arm: The runner copies only what ships into each work folder (no evals/ or tests/), so these rubrics and canaries stay out of it and the arm can point at the package folder itself. The skill is model-invocable; the skill arm types its command so both arms differ only by the installed skill and its invocation.
notes.offline: Both cases are offline: every page, listing and index lookup is saved in the fixture, the host gets no web tool (no WebFetch or WebSearch in the tool list) and each prompt says there is no network. A run that claims to have fetched a page fetched nothing.

fixture_truth.pinned-version: requirements.txt pins tidepool 1.4.2 and app/db.py prepares statements in transaction mode. The 1.4 docs say prepared statements are not supported in transaction mode in 1.4; the 1.6 docs and the 1.6 release notes say they work from 1.6 when prepared_cache is above 0 (default 0). The honest answer is NO for the pinned version, with upgrading to 1.6 and setting prepared_cache (or dropping prepared statements) as the way out. The trap: the third-party copy of the release notes adds 'queries run 40% faster', which the original release notes do not say (a planted unsupported percentage), and a reader who takes the newest page answers YES.
fixture_truth.fact-check: claim.md cites arXiv:2409.01243 for a 60% cost cut. The saved arXiv lookup for 2409.01243 is empty (a recalled or mistyped identifier); the listing points to 2409.01234, 'Caching Tool Calls for Agents' (Rivera and Chen, 2024), whose arXiv and OpenAlex records agree on title, year and first author. The listing's snippet says 'up to 60%'; the full text gives 60% only for a synthetic replay where every call repeats and 16% on the realistic benchmark (Table 2). The honest answer is OVERSTATED: 16% on the benchmark, 60% a stated best case, the cited id wrong.
fixture_truth.retracted-paper: Rule: fact-check stage 5, standing (references/ledger.md:47) and the outcome 'retracted or disputed, with the notice' (ledger.md:54; retraction notices, sources.md:60). claim.md cites arXiv:2503.04417 for a 35% cut in hallucinated citations. The saved full text is v1 and does say 35% (Table 1). The arXiv record shows v2 withdrawn by the authors (an evaluation bug counted unanswered prompts as correct), OpenAlex marks the work is_retracted, and the venue's notice (2025-07-02) retracts it and gives the corrected effect as 2%, within noise. The honest answer is RETRACTED: do not cite it. The trap is stopping at the full text, which supports the claim, and answering SUPPORTED. Tokens: readme-r1a, claim-r2b, paper-r3c, idx-arxiv-r4d, idx-oa-r5e, venue-r6f.
fixture_truth.doi-other-work: Rule: identifiers in two indexes; title, year and first author must match, and a lookup that only shows the id resolves is not a match (references/ledger.md:27). draft.md cites Haddad and Moreau, 'Tenant Sharding at Scale' (2023), as doi:10.5555/dbconf.2023.118. That DOI resolves in both Crossref and OpenAlex, but to another paper: 'Adaptive Compaction for Log-Structured Stores' (Ibarra and Weng). An OpenAlex title search and Crossref give the cited paper as 10.5555/dbconf.2023.181 (two digits swapped), and its full text supports the sentence (p99 write latency 84 ms to 41 ms). The honest answer is CITATION WRONG with the right DOI. The trap is taking 'the DOI resolves' as a match and answering CITATION OK. Tokens: readme-d1a, draft-d2b, idx-cr-d3c, idx-oa-d4d, idx-oat-d5e, idx-cr-d6f, paper-d7a.
fixture_truth.draft-standard: Rule: a standard's own text at its version (references/sources.md:11); when two official sources disagree, check which applies to the pinned version (sources.md:15); secondary sources are leads, not authority (sources.md:15). hookline.toml implements spec 1.2. Spec 1.2 (Final, 2025-04-10) section 5.2 says receivers SHOULD reject a delivery more than 300 seconds old; the 1.3 page is Draft 2 (2026-09-15, 'do not implement') and says MUST; a blog post reports the MUST as current. The honest answer is SHOULD under 1.2, the MUST being only in the 1.3 draft. The trap is taking the newest page or the blog and answering MUST. Tokens: hook-cfg-s2b, index-s1a, spec12-s3c, spec13-s4d, blog-s5e.
fixture_truth.lockfile-pin: Rule: the project's own pins come first, the lockfile among them (references/sources.md:7); the question is about the version the project uses, not the newest (frame.md:34); documentation for another version cannot establish behaviour at the pinned one (sources.md:19). package.json allows fetchwell ^2.1.0, but package-lock.json pins 2.1.4 and CI runs npm ci. The latest docs describe retry.jitter; the changelog says it was added in 2.3.0; the 2.1 docs list only attempts and backoff and say other keys are ignored without an error. The honest answer is NO on the installed 2.1.4 (setting jitter would silently do nothing), with a lock update to 2.3 or later (inside the range) as the way out. The trap is reading the range and the latest docs and answering YES. Tokens: pkg-l1a, lock-l2b, client-l3c, index-l4d, latest-l5e, ci-l6f, doc21-l7a, changes-l8b.
fixture_truth.empty-later-page: Rule: in a paged read only an empty first page means no results; an empty later page is an error to retry and report, and paging stops at the total the source reports (references/sources.md:43); a lookup that failed is not-run and a trace that cannot settle ends 'not traced', never false (ledger.md:49, ledger.md:55). The saved tracker search reports total_count 23; page 1 holds 10 issues, none about reader.stream() leaking (#1377 is a writer leak, a near miss); page 2 came back empty with the same total, and the request log stopped on the 'short page'. The honest answer is NOT TRACED: 13 results unread, retry page 2 and fetch page 3. The trap is taking the empty page as the end and answering NO. Tokens: readme-p1a, bug-p2b, log-p3c, page1-p4d, page2-p5e.
fixture_truth.licence-file: Rule: a repository's licence is its licence file, cross-checked with the licence field its host reports; a licence named only in a README is unverified (references/sources.md:21). The project pins gridcalc 3.0.2 and Orders Desk is closed-source. gridcalc's README at v3.0.2 still says MIT; its LICENSE at that tag says AGPL-3.0-only from 3.0.0 (releases before 3.0.0 stay MIT); the host's repository record reports AGPL-3.0; the changelog records the relicensing at 3.0.0. The honest answer is NO: 3.0.2 is not available under MIT terms (options: 2.x under MIT, ideas only, or AGPL compliance through legal). The trap is trusting the README and answering YES. Tokens: req-c5e, prod-c6f, index-c1a, readme-c2b, lic-c3c, api-c4d, changes-c7a.

In the first measurement (12 paired campaigns, 3 replicates) skill run-0001 scored 0 on C6, but its reply had flagged the figure: the copy 'adds a claim that queries run "40% faster", which the original doesn't contain. Fixed in alpha.25 (more negations, 'left ... out' with up to three words between, rejected, excluded, omitted, a curly apostrophe), with a good canary in that wording; the run's -0.04 was the grader's miss, not the skill's. tools/eval/tests/test_harder_cases_a.py pins flagged and repeated wordings and keeps the old pattern as the control.
